gpt_5.6_sol_high/001: The strategy uses a randomized constraint solver to sample complete enemy fleet layouts consistent with every known hit and miss. It then fires at the unknown cell occupied most often across those layouts. Samples preferentially group aligned hits into the same ship, helping finish damaged ships quickly. A placement-density heatmap provides tie-breaking and a reliable fallback if few complete layouts can be sampled within the time limit.
gpt_5.6_sol_high/002: The strategy uses a constrained Bayesian-style fleet model. It samples complete enemy fleet layouts that are consistent with every known hit and miss, weights the samples to reduce proposal bias, and fires at the unknown cell with the highest estimated ship probability. This naturally switches between hunting and pursuing hits, while accounting for ship lengths, overlap constraints, and already-completed ships. A deterministic placement-density heuristic provides tie-breaking and a legal fallback.
gpt_5.6_sol_high/003: The strategy builds a posterior model of every fleet arrangement consistent with all observed hits and misses. It uses randomized constraint solving to find valid fleets, then Gibbs-style updates—including two-ship block updates—to explore alternative placements and hit assignments. The next shot maximizes estimated ship occupancy probability, with an exact placement-density heuristic added for stability. A deterministic fallback always selects an untried cell.
gpt_5.6_sol_high/004: The strategy uses a Bayesian-style fleet model. It generates ship placements consistent with all misses and finds complete fleets covering every known hit. A Gibbs sampler then estimates the probability that each unknown cell contains a ship, naturally switching between hunt and target behavior. Multiple randomized restarts help handle touching ships and alternative hit assignments. A deterministic placement-density heuristic provides smoothing and a guaranteed legal fallback.
gpt_5.6_sol_high/005: The strategy uses a probabilistic fleet model rather than simple checkerboard firing. It generates legal placements for all remaining fleet configurations, samples complete fleets consistent with every hit and miss, and fires at the unknown cell with the highest estimated occupancy probability. A placement-density heuristic provides stable targeting when sampling is limited, strongly favoring continuations of existing hit lines while naturally abandoning ships that appear fully resolved.
